questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004554/assets/4b0c67b6a8c18b4f05198c209dae8cb960c9bfdcfc8310d0f59ee7a717e68f41.png)

Assuming that all side faces have the same height of $8\,\text{cm}$, find the total surface area of the square pyramid above using its net.
questions.worked_solution:
The net of our pyramid is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004554/assets/1fc39646f2b26116f97bc5340b0a7211911ba64ae59e4ce652bf13018fb7ef33.png)

$$

$$

First, notice that the base of the pyramid is a square with a side equal to $6\,\text{cm}.$ Hence:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=6\times 6=36\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

 

Each side face of our solid is triangle, where the base is $6\,\text{cm}$ and the height is $8\,\text{cm}.$ Therefore:

$$
\text{Area of the triangle}=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8=24\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the pyramid consists of $1$ square (base) and $4$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =(\text{Area of the square})+4\times (\text{Area of the triangle}) \\  & =36+4\times 24 \\  & =36+96 \\  & =132\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the total surface area of the cube above if it is $5\,\text{cm}$ long, $5\,\text{cm}$ wide, and $5\,\text{cm}$ tall?

First, let's consider the net of our plank.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004554/assets/efca24e18b188363ec3698ff4deaa5d5bd4ec1bdb5075138f925573a407c1f79.png)

$$

$$

From the diagram, we have squares only.

The squares are $5\,\text{cm}$ long and $5\,\text{cm}$ high. So, the area of one square is:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=5\times 5=25\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the cube consists of $6$ squares. 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =6\times (\text{Area of the square}) \\  & =6\times 25 \\  & =150\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the total surface area of the rectangular pyramid represented by the net above?
questions.worked_solution:
The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ square (base) and $4$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of the base})+4\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =1\times 150+4\times 80 \\  & =150+320 \\  & =470\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Liz deconstructs a lantern and gets the net shown above. In the figure, the areas of two of its faces are shown. What is the total surface area of the lantern?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a triangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ triangle (base) and $3$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of the base})+3\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =1\times 5+3\times 13 \\  & =5+39 \\  & =44\,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

An artist makes a glass sculpture. In the figure, the areas of some of the faces are displayed in a net of the sculpture. What is the total surface area of the sculpture?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a triangular prism. The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ triangles (base and top) and $3$ rectangles (central and side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+3\times (\text{Area of the side faces}) \\  & =2\times 8+3\times 17 \\  & =16+51 \\  & =67\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
